**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling:

- **§3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the only section binding us with prohibitions — is confined to ordinary licence hygiene: no copying beyond backups, no transfer/sublicence, no reverse engineering, and "not use the Work except as authorized herein." Nothing touches what businesses we run or what products we buy or build.
- **§2 (Grant of License)** is a non-exclusive licence with no exclusivity, minimum-purchase, or sole-source commitment on us.
- **§14 (Confidentiality)** expressly carves out independently developed information (p0098), so it does not operate as a back-door restraint on internal development.
- **§19** is a mutual, one-year employee non-solicit — a different category, reciprocal, and not a restriction on our business lines.
- Text sweeps for "compet", "similar", "exclusive", and "shall not develop/market/sell/engage/acquire/distribute" surfaced no restrictive covenant binding us (the only "compet" hit was "competence" in §9).

This sits at the rule's **preferred** position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so nothing to negotiate here.
